requirements.summary: The same two files remained present, with unchanged sizes and SHA-256 hashes before repair, after repair, and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the existing inventory data is owned by inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: Every entry in the inventory tree was directly observed with inventorysvc ownership after repair and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Make the inventory data readable by inventory-readers.
requirements.summary: Directories and files had appropriate group permissions, and a non-owner process using only the inventory-readers GID successfully read and hashed both files before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Make /srv/inventory inaccessible to users outside the owner and inventory-readers group.
requirements.summary: All entries had empty other permissions, and an unrelated UID/GID was directly denied both directory listing and file reading before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, the restart was acknowledged, a different boot ID was observed, and system, filesystem, identities, data, permissions, reader access, and outsider denial all recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently confirm the boot transition.
limitations: Requirement preserve-contents cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: Chronological review found no unnecessary mutations. Creating the missing group and service account was a necessary prerequisite; changing ownership and modes implemented the repair; and the transient reboot request served the mandatory restart protocol. No unwanted residue, failed services, new exposure, or package damage was observed. The interrupted status command coincided with reboot and was read-only. Restart-related PID and systemd-private-directory changes are expected, while sockets, service health, and package health recovered normally.
